title: Job 28
paragraphs: ¹ Surely there are mines where silver is found, and places where gold is refined. ² Iron is smelted from the earth, and copper is poured from stone. ³ Miners push back the darkness, searching the deepest shafts — rock in the shadow of death. ⁴ They sink a shaft far from where people live, forgotten by those who walk above; they hang there, swaying away from the rest. ⁵ As for the earth — bread comes from its surface, but underneath it is churned up as if by fire.

⁶ Its rocks hold sapphires, and its dust is flecked with gold. ⁷ No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon's eye has ever seen it. ⁸ No proud beast has walked it, no lion has ever crossed it. ⁹ The miner reaches into the hardest rock and overturns mountains at the root. ¹⁰ He cuts channels through the stone; his eyes catch every gleaming thing.

¹¹ He dams up the streams so they don't trickle through, and brings hidden things into the light. ¹² But where can wisdom be found? Where does understanding dwell? ¹³ No living person knows what it is worth; it cannot be found in the land of the living. ¹⁴ The deep says, "It is not in me," and the sea says, "It is not with me." ¹⁵ It cannot be bought with gold, and no amount of silver can pay its price.

¹⁶ It cannot be weighed against the gold of Ophir, nor against precious onyx or sapphire. ¹⁷ Gold and glass cannot match it, nor can it be traded for vessels of fine gold. ¹⁸ Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies. ¹⁹ The topaz of Ethiopia cannot equal it, and it cannot be valued against pure gold. ²⁰ Where, then, does wisdom come from? Where does understanding live?

²¹ It is hidden from the eyes of every living creature, concealed even from the birds of the sky. ²² Destruction and Death say, "We have heard only rumors of it." ²³ God alone knows the way to it; only he knows where it dwells. ²⁴ For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under heaven. ²⁵ He determined the weight of the wind and measured out the waters.

²⁶ When he set a limit for the rain and marked a path for the thunderstorm, ²⁷ then he saw wisdom and examined it; he confirmed it and tested it thoroughly. ²⁸ And to humanity he said, "The fear of the LORD — that is wisdom. To turn away from evil is understanding."
